--src: Mathlib.Data.Set.Finite.Basic
@[simp]
theorem infinite_union {s t : Set α} : (s ∪ t).Infinite ↔ s.Infinite ∨ t.Infinite := by
  simp only [Set.Infinite, finite_union, not_and_or]

--src: Mathlib.Data.Finite.Card
theorem eq_of_subset_of_card_le (ht : t.Finite) (hsub : s ⊆ t) (hcard : Nat.card t ≤ Nat.card s) :
    s = t :=
  (eq_or_ssubset_of_subset hsub).elim id fun h ↦ absurd hcard <| not_le_of_lt <| ht.card_lt_card h

--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Cardinal.Basic
theorem mk_union_le_aleph0 {α} {P Q : Set α} :
    #(P ∪ Q : Set α) ≤ ℵ₀ ↔ #P ≤ ℵ₀ ∧ #Q ≤ ℵ₀ := by
  simp only [le_aleph0_iff_subtype_countable, mem_union, setOf_mem_eq, Set.union_def,
    ← countable_union]

--src: Mathlib.Data.Set.Finite.Basic
lemma Finite.exists_not_mem (hs : s.Finite) : ∃ a, a ∉ s := by
  by_contra! h; exact infinite_univ (hs.subset fun a _ ↦ h _)

--src: Mathlib.Data.Set.Finite.Basic
theorem Infinite.diff {s t : Set α} (hs : s.Infinite) (ht : t.Finite) : (s \ t).Infinite := fun h =>
  hs <| h.of_diff ht

--src: Mathlib.Data.Set.Finite.Basic
theorem Finite.union {s t : Set α} (hs : s.Finite) (ht : t.Finite) : (s ∪ t).Finite := by
  rw [Set.Finite] at hs ht
  apply toFinite

--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Cardinal.Basic
theorem mk_insert_le {α : Type u} {s : Set α} {a : α} : #(insert a s : Set α) ≤ #s + 1 := by
  by_cases h : a ∈ s
  · simp only [insert_eq_of_mem h, self_le_add_right]
  · rw [mk_insert h]

--src: Mathlib.Data.Finite.Card
theorem card_union_le (s t : Set α) : Nat.card (↥(s ∪ t)) ≤ Nat.card s + Nat.card t := by
  cases' _root_.finite_or_infinite (↥(s ∪ t)) with h h
  · rw [finite_coe_iff, finite_union, ← finite_coe_iff, ← finite_coe_iff] at h
    cases h
    rw [← @Nat.cast_le Cardinal, Nat.cast_add, Finite.cast_card_eq_mk, Finite.cast_card_eq_mk,
      Finite.cast_card_eq_mk]
    exact Cardinal.mk_union_le s t
  · exact Nat.card_eq_zero_of_infinite.trans_le (zero_le _)

--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Cardinal.Basic
lemma aleph0_le_mk_iff : ℵ₀ ≤ #α ↔ Infinite α := infinite_iff.symm

--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Cardinal.Arithmetic
theorem mk_bounded_subset_le {α : Type u} (s : Set α) (c : Cardinal.{u}) :
    #{ t : Set α // t ⊆ s ∧ #t ≤ c } ≤ max #s ℵ₀ ^ c := by
  refine le_trans ?_ (mk_bounded_set_le s c)
  refine ⟨Embedding.codRestrict _ ?_ ?_⟩
  · use fun t => (↑) ⁻¹' t.1
    rintro ⟨t, ht1, ht2⟩ ⟨t', h1t', h2t'⟩ h
    apply Subtype.eq
    dsimp only at h ⊢
    refine (preimage_eq_preimage' ?_ ?_).1 h <;> rw [Subtype.range_coe] <;> assumption
  rintro ⟨t, _, h2t⟩; exact (mk_preimage_of_injective _ _ Subtype.val_injective).trans h2t

C1_dependencies.name: Disjoint
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- Two elements of a lattice are disjoint if their inf is the bottom element.
  (This generalizes disjoint sets, viewed as members of the subset lattice.)

Note that we define this without reference to `⊓`, as this allows us to talk about orders where
the infimum is not unique, or where implementing `Inf` would require additional `Decidable`
arguments. -/
def Disjoint (a b : α) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ≤ a → x ≤ b → x ≤ ⊥

C1_dependencies.name: Set
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- A set is a collection of elements of some type `α`.

Although `Set` is defined as `α → Prop`, this is an implementation detail which should not be
relied on. Instead, `setOf` and membership of a set (`∈`) should be used to convert between sets
and predicates.
-/
def Set (α : Type u) := α → Prop

C0_dependencies.content:
theorem le_card_categorise {r : Rel α α} (R : OrbitRestriction (r.dom ∪ r.codom) β) (b : β) :
    #((r.dom ∪ r.codom : Set α) × ℕ) ≤ #(R.sandbox ∩ R.categorise ⁻¹' {b} : Set α) := by
  rw [Cardinal.mk_prod, Cardinal.lift_id', Cardinal.mk_eq_aleph0 ℕ, Cardinal.lift_aleph0]
  refine le_trans ?_ (R.le_card_categorise b)
  apply mul_le_of_le
  · exact le_max_left ℵ₀ _
  · exact le_max_right ℵ₀ _
  · exact le_max_left ℵ₀ _

C0_dependencies.content:
theorem catInj_injective {r : Rel α α} {R : OrbitRestriction (r.dom ∪ r.codom) β}
    {b₁ b₂ : β} {x₁ x₂ : (r.dom ∪ r.codom : Set α) × ℕ}
    (h : (catInj R b₁ x₁ : α) = catInj R b₂ x₂) :
    b₁ = b₂ ∧ x₁ = x₂ := by
  have h₁ := categorise_catInj R b₁ x₁
  have h₂ := categorise_catInj R b₂ x₂
  rw [h, h₂] at h₁
  cases h₁
  rw [Subtype.coe_inj, EmbeddingLike.apply_eq_iff_eq] at h
  exact ⟨rfl, h⟩

    #(r.permutativeExtension R).dom ≤ max ℵ₀ #r.dom := by
  apply (mk_le_mk_of_subset (dom_permutativeExtension_subset' r R)).trans
  apply (mk_union_le _ _).trans
  apply (add_le_add (mk_union_le _ _) (mk_union_le _ _)).trans
  apply add_le_of_le (le_max_left _ _) <;> apply add_le_of_le (le_max_left _ _)
  · exact le_max_right _ _
  · exact le_max_of_le_right (card_codom_le_of_coinjective hr)
  · refine (mk_biUnion_le_of_le (max ℵ₀ #r.dom) ?_).trans ?_
    · intro a _
      have := mk_iUnion_le_of_le_lift

theorem permutativeExtension_codomEqDom {r : Rel α α} (R : OrbitRestriction (r.dom ∪ r.codom) β) :
    (permutativeExtension r R).CodomEqDom := by
  rw [codomEqDom_iff']
  constructor
  · rintro a₁ a₂ (h | h)
    · by_cases had : a₂ ∈ r.dom
      · obtain ⟨a₃, h'⟩ := had
        exact ⟨a₃, Or.inl h'⟩
      · exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.right a₂ had ⟨a₁, h⟩)⟩
    · cases h with
      | left _ had hac =>
        obtain ⟨a₃, h⟩ := had
        exact ⟨a₃, Or.inl h⟩
      | leftStep n a had hac =>
        cases n with
        | zero => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.left a had hac)⟩
        | succ n => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.leftStep n a had hac)⟩
      | right _ had hac => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.rightStep 0 a₁ had hac)⟩
      | rightStep n a had hac => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.rightStep (n + 1) a had hac)⟩
  · rintro a₁ a₂ (h | h)
    · by_cases hac : a₁ ∈ r.codom
      · obtain ⟨a₃, h'⟩ := hac
        exact ⟨a₃, Or.inl h'⟩
      · exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.left a₁ ⟨a₂, h⟩ hac)⟩
    · cases h with
      | left _ had hac => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.leftStep 0 a₂ had hac)⟩
      | leftStep n a had hac => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.leftStep (n + 1) a had hac)⟩
      | right _ had hac =>
        obtain ⟨a₃, h⟩ := hac
        exact ⟨a₃, Or.inl h⟩
      | rightStep n a had hac =>
        cases n with
        | zero => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.right a had hac)⟩
        | succ n => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.rightStep n a had hac)⟩

C1_dependencies.name: Disjoint
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- Two elements of a lattice are disjoint if their inf is the bottom element.
  (This generalizes disjoint sets, viewed as members of the subset lattice.)

Note that we define this without reference to `⊓`, as this allows us to talk about orders where
the infimum is not unique, or where implementing `Inf` would require additional `Decidable`
arguments. -/
def Disjoint (a b : α) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ≤ a → x ≤ b → x ≤ ⊥

C1_dependencies.name: Disjoint
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- Two elements of a lattice are disjoint if their inf is the bottom element.
  (This generalizes disjoint sets, viewed as members of the subset lattice.)

Note that we define this without reference to `⊓`, as this allows us to talk about orders where
the infimum is not unique, or where implementing `Inf` would require additional `Decidable`
arguments. -/
def Disjoint (a b : α) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ≤ a → x ≤ b → x ≤ ⊥

  clear_value a₄
  rw [h] at h₁
  cases h₁ with
  | left _ hac had =>
    cases h₂ with
    | left => cases h; rfl
    | _ => cases catInj_ne_of_mem R _ _ a₃ (Or.inl hac) h
  | leftStep =>
    cases h₂ with
    | left _ hac had => cases catInj_ne_of_mem R _ _ a₄ (Or.inl hac) h.symm

      simp only [Function.comp_apply, catInj_inj, add_left_inj, Function.iterate_succ_apply',

      exact ⟨h.1.symm, h.2.1.symm, h.2.2.symm⟩

    cases h₂ with
    | left _ ha₄c ha₄d => cases catInj_ne_of_mem R _ _ a₄ (Or.inl ha₄c) h.symm

      rw [catInj_inj] at h
      cases h.2.1

    | right =>

    | rightStep => simp only [catInj_inj, AddLeftCancelMonoid.add_eq_zero,
        one_ne_zero, and_false] at h
  | rightStep =>
    cases h₂ with
    | left _ hac had => cases catInj_ne_of_mem R _ _ a₄ (Or.inl hac) h.symm
    | leftStep =>
      rw [catInj_inj] at h
      cases h.2.1

    | rightStep =>
      simp only [Function.comp_apply, catInj_inj, add_left_inj, Function.iterate_succ_apply',

      exact ⟨h.1.symm, h.2.1.symm, h.2.2.symm⟩

      simp only [catInj_inj, self_eq_add_left, AddLeftCancelMonoid.add_eq_zero,

theorem permutativeExtension_codomEqDom {r : Rel α α} (R : OrbitRestriction (r.dom ∪ r.codom) β) :
    (permutativeExtension r R).CodomEqDom := by
  rw [codomEqDom_iff']
  constructor
  · rintro a₁ a₂ (h | h)
    · by_cases had : a₂ ∈ r.dom
      · obtain ⟨a₃, h'⟩ := had
        exact ⟨a₃, Or.inl h'⟩
      · exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.right a₂ had ⟨a₁, h⟩)⟩
    · cases h with
      | left _ had hac =>
        obtain ⟨a₃, h⟩ := had
        exact ⟨a₃, Or.inl h⟩
      | leftStep n a had hac =>
        cases n with
        | zero => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.left a had hac)⟩
        | succ n => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.leftStep n a had hac)⟩
      | right _ had hac => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.rightStep 0 a₁ had hac)⟩
      | rightStep n a had hac => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.rightStep (n + 1) a had hac)⟩
  · rintro a₁ a₂ (h | h)
    · by_cases hac : a₁ ∈ r.codom
      · obtain ⟨a₃, h'⟩ := hac
        exact ⟨a₃, Or.inl h'⟩
      · exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.left a₁ ⟨a₂, h⟩ hac)⟩
    · cases h with
      | left _ had hac => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.leftStep 0 a₂ had hac)⟩
      | leftStep n a had hac => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.leftStep (n + 1) a had hac)⟩
      | right _ had hac =>
        obtain ⟨a₃, h⟩ := hac
        exact ⟨a₃, Or.inl h⟩
      | rightStep n a had hac =>
        cases n with
        | zero => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.right a had hac)⟩
        | succ n => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.rightStep n a had hac)⟩

C1_dependencies.content:
/-- Two elements of a lattice are disjoint if their inf is the bottom element.
  (This generalizes disjoint sets, viewed as members of the subset lattice.)

Note that we define this without reference to `⊓`, as this allows us to talk about orders where
the infimum is not unique, or where implementing `Inf` would require additional `Decidable`
arguments. -/
def Disjoint (a b : α) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ≤ a → x ≤ b → x ≤ ⊥

  rw [codomEqDom_iff']
  constructor
  · rintro a₁ a₂ (h | h)
    · by_cases had : a₂ ∈ r.dom
      · obtain ⟨a₃, h'⟩ := had
        exact ⟨a₃, Or.inl h'⟩
      · exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.right a₂ had ⟨a₁, h⟩)⟩
    · cases h with
      | left _ had hac =>
        obtain ⟨a₃, h⟩ := had
        exact ⟨a₃, Or.inl h⟩
      | leftStep n a had hac =>
        cases n with
        | zero => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.left a had hac)⟩
        | succ n => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.leftStep n a had hac)⟩
      | right _ had hac => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.rightStep 0 a₁ had hac)⟩
      | rightStep n a had hac => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.rightStep (n + 1) a had hac)⟩
  · rintro a₁ a₂ (h | h)
    · by_cases hac : a₁ ∈ r.codom
      · obtain ⟨a₃, h'⟩ := hac
        exact ⟨a₃, Or.inl h'⟩
      · exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.left a₁ ⟨a₂, h⟩ hac)⟩
    · cases h with
      | left _ had hac => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.leftStep 0 a₂ had hac)⟩
      | leftStep n a had hac => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.leftStep (n + 1) a had hac)⟩
      | right _ had hac =>
        obtain ⟨a₃, h⟩ := hac
        exact ⟨a₃, Or.inl h⟩
      | rightStep n a had hac =>
        cases n with

C0_dependencies.name: Rel.le_card_categorise
C0_dependencies.content:
theorem le_card_categorise {r : Rel α α} (R : OrbitRestriction (r.dom ∪ r.codom) β) (b : β) :
    #((r.dom ∪ r.codom : Set α) × ℕ) ≤ #(R.sandbox ∩ R.categorise ⁻¹' {b} : Set α) := by
  rw [Cardinal.mk_prod, Cardinal.lift_id', Cardinal.mk_eq_aleph0 ℕ, Cardinal.lift_aleph0]
  refine le_trans ?_ (R.le_card_categorise b)
  apply mul_le_of_le
  · exact le_max_left ℵ₀ _
  · exact le_max_right ℵ₀ _
  · exact le_max_left ℵ₀ _

C0_dependencies.name: Rel.catInj_ne_of_mem
C0_dependencies.content:
theorem catInj_ne_of_mem {r : Rel α α} (R : OrbitRestriction (r.dom ∪ r.codom) β) (b : β)
    (x : (r.dom ∪ r.codom : Set α) × ℕ) (a : α) (ha : a ∈ r.dom ∪ r.codom) :
    (catInj R b x : α) ≠ a := by
  have := R.sandbox_disjoint
  rw [Set.disjoint_iff_forall_ne] at this
  exact (this ha (catInj_mem_sandbox R b x)).symm

C0_dependencies.name: Rel.catInj_injective
C0_dependencies.content:
theorem catInj_injective {r : Rel α α} {R : OrbitRestriction (r.dom ∪ r.codom) β}
    {b₁ b₂ : β} {x₁ x₂ : (r.dom ∪ r.codom : Set α) × ℕ}
    (h : (catInj R b₁ x₁ : α) = catInj R b₂ x₂) :
    b₁ = b₂ ∧ x₁ = x₂ := by
  have h₁ := categorise_catInj R b₁ x₁
  have h₂ := categorise_catInj R b₂ x₂
  rw [h, h₂] at h₁
  cases h₁
  rw [Subtype.coe_inj, EmbeddingLike.apply_eq_iff_eq] at h
  exact ⟨rfl, h⟩

C0_dependencies.content:
@[simp]
theorem catInj_inj {r : Rel α α} {R : OrbitRestriction (r.dom ∪ r.codom) β}
    {b₁ b₂ : β} {a₁ a₂ : α} {h₁ : a₁ ∈ r.dom ∪ r.codom} {h₂ : a₂ ∈ r.dom ∪ r.codom} {n₁ n₂ : ℕ} :
    (catInj R b₁ (⟨a₁, h₁⟩, n₁) : α) = catInj R b₂ (⟨a₂, h₂⟩, n₂) ↔
      b₁ = b₂ ∧ a₁ = a₂ ∧ n₁ = n₂ := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨rfl, h'⟩ := catInj_injective h
    cases h'
    exact ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl⟩
  · rintro ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl⟩
    rfl

        (catInj R (R.catPerm^[n + 2] (R.categorise a)) (⟨a, Or.inr hac⟩, n + 1))

  clear_value a₄
  rw [h] at h₁
  cases h₁ with
  | left _ hac had =>
    cases h₂ with
    | left => cases h; rfl
    | _ => cases catInj_ne_of_mem R _ _ a₃ (Or.inl hac) h

    cases h₂ with
    | left _ hac had => cases catInj_ne_of_mem R _ _ a₄ (Or.inl hac) h.symm

      rw [catInj_inj] at h

    | right =>

  | rightStep =>
    cases h₂ with
    | left _ hac had => cases catInj_ne_of_mem R _ _ a₄ (Or.inl hac) h.symm
    | leftStep =>
      rw [catInj_inj] at h

    | right =>
      simp only [catInj_inj, self_eq_add_left, AddLeftCancelMonoid.add_eq_zero,

  constructor

      · obtain ⟨a₃, h'⟩ := had
        exact ⟨a₃, Or.inl h'⟩
      · exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.right a₂ had ⟨a₁, h⟩)⟩
    · cases h with
      | left _ had hac =>
        obtain ⟨a₃, h⟩ := had

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

C1_dependencies.name: Disjoint
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- Two elements of a lattice are disjoint if their inf is the bottom element.
  (This generalizes disjoint sets, viewed as members of the subset lattice.)

Note that we define this without reference to `⊓`, as this allows us to talk about orders where
the infimum is not unique, or where implementing `Inf` would require additional `Decidable`
arguments. -/
def Disjoint (a b : α) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ≤ a → x ≤ b → x ≤ ⊥

theorem permutativeExtension_codomEqDom {r : Rel α α} (R : OrbitRestriction (r.dom ∪ r.codom) β) :
    (permutativeExtension r R).CodomEqDom := by
  rw [codomEqDom_iff']
  constructor
  · rintro a₁ a₂ (h | h)
    · by_cases had : a₂ ∈ r.dom
      · obtain ⟨a₃, h'⟩ := had
        exact ⟨a₃, Or.inl h'⟩
      · exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.right a₂ had ⟨a₁, h⟩)⟩
    · cases h with
      | left _ had hac =>
        obtain ⟨a₃, h⟩ := had
        exact ⟨a₃, Or.inl h⟩
      | leftStep n a had hac =>
        cases n with
        | zero => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.left a had hac)⟩
        | succ n => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.leftStep n a had hac)⟩
      | right _ had hac => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.rightStep 0 a₁ had hac)⟩
      | rightStep n a had hac => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.rightStep (n + 1) a had hac)⟩
  · rintro a₁ a₂ (h | h)
    · by_cases hac : a₁ ∈ r.codom
      · obtain ⟨a₃, h'⟩ := hac
        exact ⟨a₃, Or.inl h'⟩
      · exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.left a₁ ⟨a₂, h⟩ hac)⟩
    · cases h with
      | left _ had hac => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.leftStep 0 a₂ had hac)⟩
      | leftStep n a had hac => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.leftStep (n + 1) a had hac)⟩
      | right _ had hac =>
        obtain ⟨a₃, h⟩ := hac
        exact ⟨a₃, Or.inl h⟩
      | rightStep n a had hac =>
        cases n with
        | zero => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.right a had hac)⟩
        | succ n => exact ⟨_, Or.inr (newOrbits.rightStep n a had hac)⟩

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

C1_dependencies.name: Disjoint
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- Two elements of a lattice are disjoint if their inf is the bottom element.
  (This generalizes disjoint sets, viewed as members of the subset lattice.)

Note that we define this without reference to `⊓`, as this allows us to talk about orders where
the infimum is not unique, or where implementing `Inf` would require additional `Decidable`
arguments. -/
def Disjoint (a b : α) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ≤ a → x ≤ b → x ≤ ⊥

  exact ⟨rfl, h⟩

  intro a₁ a₂ a₃ h₁ h₂
  set a₄ := a₃ with h
  clear_value a₄
  rw [h] at h₁
  cases h₁ with
  | left _ hac had =>
    cases h₂ with
    | left => cases h; rfl
    | _ => cases catInj_ne_of_mem R _ _ a₃ (Or.inl hac) h
  | leftStep =>
    cases h₂ with
    | left _ hac had => cases catInj_ne_of_mem R _ _ a₄ (Or.inl hac) h.symm
    | leftStep =>
      simp only [Function.comp_apply, catInj_inj, add_left_inj, Function.iterate_succ_apply',
        EmbeddingLike.apply_eq_iff_eq] at h ⊢
      exact ⟨h.1.symm, h.2.1.symm, h.2.2.symm⟩
    | _ =>
      rw [catInj_inj] at h
      cases h.2.1
      contradiction
  | right _ ha₁c ha₁d =>
    cases h₂ with
    | left _ ha₄c ha₄d => cases catInj_ne_of_mem R _ _ a₄ (Or.inl ha₄c) h.symm
    | leftStep n a had hac =>
      rw [catInj_inj] at h
      cases h.2.1
      contradiction
    | right =>
      rw [catInj_inj] at h
      exact h.2.1.symm
    | rightStep => simp only [catInj_inj, AddLeftCancelMonoid.add_eq_zero,
        one_ne_zero, and_false] at h
  | rightStep =>
    cases h₂ with
    | left _ hac had => cases catInj_ne_of_mem R _ _ a₄ (Or.inl hac) h.symm
    | leftStep =>
      rw [catInj_inj] at h
      cases h.2.1
      contradiction
    | rightStep =>
      simp only [Function.comp_apply, catInj_inj, add_left_inj, Function.iterate_succ_apply',
        EmbeddingLike.apply_eq_iff_eq] at h ⊢
      exact ⟨h.1.symm, h.2.1.symm, h.2.2.symm⟩
    | right =>
      simp only [catInj_inj, self_eq_add_left, AddLeftCancelMonoid.add_eq_zero,
        one_ne_zero, and_false] at h

  exact ⟨rfl, h⟩

C0_dependencies.name: Rel.catInj_injective
C0_dependencies.content:
theorem catInj_injective {r : Rel α α} {R : OrbitRestriction (r.dom ∪ r.codom) β}
    {b₁ b₂ : β} {x₁ x₂ : (r.dom ∪ r.codom : Set α) × ℕ}
    (h : (catInj R b₁ x₁ : α) = catInj R b₂ x₂) :
    b₁ = b₂ ∧ x₁ = x₂ := by
  have h₁ := categorise_catInj R b₁ x₁
  have h₂ := categorise_catInj R b₂ x₂
  rw [h, h₂] at h₁
  cases h₁
  rw [Subtype.coe_inj, EmbeddingLike.apply_eq_iff_eq] at h
  exact ⟨rfl, h⟩

  have h₁ := categorise_catInj R b₁ x₁

  rw [Subtype.coe_inj, EmbeddingLike.apply_eq_iff_eq] at h
  exact ⟨rfl, h⟩

    #((r.dom ∪ r.codom : Set α) × ℕ) ≤ #(R.sandbox ∩ R.categorise ⁻¹' {b} : Set α) := by
  rw [Cardinal.mk_prod, Cardinal.lift_id', Cardinal.mk_eq_aleph0 ℕ, Cardinal.lift_aleph0]
  refine le_trans ?_ (R.le_card_categorise b)
  apply mul_le_of_le
  · exact le_max_left ℵ₀ _
  · exact le_max_right ℵ₀ _
  · exact le_max_left ℵ₀ _

  have h₁ := categorise_catInj R b₁ x₁

  exact ⟨rfl, h⟩

/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

theorem image_eq_dom_of_codomain_subset {s : Set β} (h : r.codom ⊆ s) : r.preimage s = r.dom := by
  rw [← preimage_univ]
  apply Set.eq_of_subset_of_subset

theorem image_eq_dom_of_codomain_subset {s : Set β} (h : r.codom ⊆ s) : r.preimage s = r.dom := by
  rw [← preimage_univ]
  apply Set.eq_of_subset_of_subset
  · exact image_subset _ (Set.subset_univ _)
  · intro x hx
    simp only [mem_preimage, Set.mem_univ, true_and] at hx
    rcases hx with ⟨y, ryx⟩
    have hy : y ∈ s := h ⟨x, ryx⟩
    exact ⟨y, ⟨hy, ryx⟩⟩

  apply Set.eq_of_subset_of_subset
  · apply r.image_mono (by simp)
  · intro x h
    rw [mem_image] at *
    rcases h with ⟨y, hy, ryx⟩
    use y

    rw [dom, Set.mem_setOf_eq]
    use x

  exact ⟨rfl, h⟩

/-- When a list of the form `[...xs, sep, ...as]` is split on `p`, the first element is `xs`,

theorem splitOnP_first (h : ∀ x ∈ xs, ¬p x) (sep : α) (hsep : p sep) (as : List α) :

theorem le_card_categorise {r : Rel α α} (R : OrbitRestriction (r.dom ∪ r.codom) β) (b : β) :
    #((r.dom ∪ r.codom : Set α) × ℕ) ≤ #(R.sandbox ∩ R.categorise ⁻¹' {b} : Set α) := by
  rw [Cardinal.mk_prod, Cardinal.lift_id', Cardinal.mk_eq_aleph0 ℕ, Cardinal.lift_aleph0]
  refine le_trans ?_ (R.le_card_categorise b)

    #((r.dom ∪ r.codom : Set α) × ℕ) ≤ #(R.sandbox ∩ R.categorise ⁻¹' {b} : Set α) := by
  rw [Cardinal.mk_prod, Cardinal.lift_id', Cardinal.mk_eq_aleph0 ℕ, Cardinal.lift_aleph0]
  refine le_trans ?_ (R.le_card_categorise b)
  apply mul_le_of_le
  · exact le_max_left ℵ₀ _
  · exact le_max_right ℵ₀ _
  · exact le_max_left ℵ₀ _

    {b₁ b₂ : β} {x₁ x₂ : (r.dom ∪ r.codom : Set α) × ℕ}
    (h : (catInj R b₁ x₁ : α) = catInj R b₂ x₂) :

  have h₁ := categorise_catInj R b₁ x₁
  have h₂ := categorise_catInj R b₂ x₂
  rw [h, h₂] at h₁
  cases h₁
  rw [Subtype.coe_inj, EmbeddingLike.apply_eq_iff_eq] at h
  exact ⟨rfl, h⟩

  exact ⟨rfl, h⟩

/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

/-- The infinite pigeonhole principle -/
theorem infinite_pigeonhole {β α : Type u} (f : β → α) (h₁ : ℵ₀ ≤ #β) (h₂ : #α < (#β).ord.cof) :
    ∃ a : α, #(f ⁻¹' {a}) = #β := by
  have : ∃ a, #β ≤ #(f ⁻¹' {a}) := by
    by_contra! h
    apply mk_univ.not_lt
    rw [← preimage_univ, ← iUnion_of_singleton, preimage_iUnion]
    exact
      mk_iUnion_le_sum_mk.trans_lt
        ((sum_le_iSup _).trans_lt <| mul_lt_of_lt h₁ (h₂.trans_le <| cof_ord_le _) (iSup_lt h₂ h))
  cases' this with x h
  refine ⟨x, h.antisymm' ?_⟩
  rw [le_mk_iff_exists_set]
  exact ⟨_, rfl⟩

    sum_le_sum _ _ hf

/-- The type of flags, aka maximal chains, of an order. -/
structure Flag (α : Type*) [LE α] where
  /-- The `carrier` of a flag is the underlying set. -/
  carrier : Set α
  /-- By definition, a flag is a chain -/
  Chain' : IsChain (· ≤ ·) carrier
  /-- By definition, a flag is a maximal chain -/
  max_chain' : ∀ ⦃s⦄, IsChain (· ≤ ·) s → carrier ⊆ s → carrier = s

--src: Mathlib.Order.Chain
protected theorem le_or_le (s : Flag α) (ha : a ∈ s) (hb : b ∈ s) : a ≤ b ∨ b ≤ a :=
  s.chain_le.total ha hb

--src: Mathlib.Data.List.Basic
theorem getElem_succ_scanl {i : ℕ} (h : i + 1 < (scanl f b l).length) :
    (scanl f b l)[i + 1] =
      f ((scanl f b l)[i]'(Nat.lt_of_succ_lt h))
        (l[i]'(Nat.lt_of_succ_lt_succ (h.trans_eq (length_scanl b l)))) := by
  induction i generalizing b l with
  | zero =>
    cases l
    · simp only [scanl, length, zero_eq, lt_self_iff_false] at h
    · simp
  | succ i hi =>
    cases l
    · simp only [scanl, length] at h
      exact absurd h (by omega)
    · simp_rw [scanl_cons]
      rw [getElem_append_right]
      · simp only [length, Nat.zero_add 1, succ_add_sub_one, hi]; rfl
      · simp only [length_singleton]; omega

    _ = Finset.univ.sup (pair x y).obj := by rw [finite_colimit_eq_finset_univ_sup (pair x y)]
